Header: POC weekly sync — Pilot capacity gating, autoscale policy & burst playbook
Date/Time: Tue Aug 4 2026 11:00 AM PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jamal Ortiz (Redwood SE), Anita Rao (Crestline Head of Platform), Tom Becker (SRE Lead), Sofia Marin (Security), Luis Chen (Product)
Links shared: dedicated-sizing-v2.xlsx, burst-runbook-draft.md, security-checklist.pdf

Summary: Quick readout from this week's staging run, discussion of autoscale thresholds and gating rules, agreement on a burst rehearsal window and security signoff timeline.

Topics: results review; autoscale policy tuning; burst gating; failover to hosted variants; SOC2/KMS questions

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we've got 45 minutes, quick agenda — jamal will walk the staging run results then we'll talk autoscale gating and next steps.
[00:12] Jamal Ortiz: Cool. So, um, staging run last night, we did three 10-minute sustained peaks, stepping from 800 to 2.4k RPS, with 95th around 220ms on the p100 nodes, and a few tail blips to 480ms during GC windows. Note: the transcript's numbers come from the load generator.
[00:29] Tom Becker: Wait, p100? I thought we were testing on 4090s — our csv says A4000s. There's a mismatch between the infra tag and the runner.
[00:36] Jamal Ortiz: Right, the runner got labeled automatically, sorry, it's 4090s, not p100, my bad. The important takeaway is CPU vs GPU saturation — GPU memory pressure hit 78% during the 2.4k spike, KV cache hit rate dipped to 64%.
[00:50] Anita Rao: Can you explain KV cache dip a little more? Is that the prefix caching you mentioned earlier?
[00:56] Jamal Ortiz: Yeah, it's the prefix/K V cache — so cold prefixes during synthetic traces caused more token decoding work, which increased per-token latency. In production your distribution shows more steady prefixes so we expect better hit rates but we need your trace.
[01:12] Luis Chen: Quick note — our prod trace has a bi-modal distribution, like big spikes when batch jobs finish and push events. We can scrub and share.
[01:19] Jamal Ortiz: Perfect, please send.
[01:21] Maya Patel: Alright on autoscale policy, we proposed a two-tier policy: base fleet for steady-state (target 700 RPS) and burst pool that scales up based on queue length and GPU util > 70% for two consecutive minutes. Questions?
[01:36] Tom Becker: How deterministic is the scale-up time? If we need to jump from 700 to 2.4k, what's the expected warmup — minutes or seconds?
[01:43] Jamal Ortiz: Realistic is 90-180s to spin up additional capacity in Dedicated if using pre-warmed instances; if cold provisioning from zero it could be 6-8 minutes. We recommend reserved minimal burst instances pre-warmed during business hours.
[01:58] Sofia Marin: From a security/compliance perspective we need to avoid shared-hosted fallback for certain PHI payloads. Does Redwood have region-specific VPC options and guaranteed no-host fallback?
[02:08] Maya Patel: Yes, for the Private/Dedicated offering you can pin to a VPC and we can disable automatic fallback to hosted variants; that said, in our plan we put a safe fallback but we can remove it for your sensitive routes.
[02:20] Sofia Marin: Also KMS — we need HSM-backed keys for token encryption and audit logs for inference requests.
[02:26] Jamal Ortiz: We do KMS with HSM integrations and per-request audit logs that can stream to your SIEM; we'll attach the compliance appendix.
[02:34] Anita Rao: One objection — your cost model for pre-warmed burst instances looks expensive. Can you show incremental cost per 1k QPS for our model?
[02:41] Maya Patel: Yes, we'll send an incremental cost table. The Optimize recommendations can reduce that via quantization profiles and batching — tradeoff is slight quality delta on generated text.
[02:52] Tom Becker: How much quality delta on quantization? Our medical summarization is sensitive.
[02:56] Jamal Ortiz: For 4-bit quant on our curated model you might see 1-2% BLEU-ish drop — sorry BLEU isn't the right metric, but you know, subtle changes. We recommend running a small eval against your prompt set first.
[03:10] Maya Patel: Ok let's lock the burst rehearsal: tentative window Friday Aug 13 09:00-10:30 PT. Jamal will run the replay script, customer will be on call and monitor app telemetry.
[03:20] Jamal Ortiz: On gating rules, we also suggest a queue-length circuit breaker: if queue > 10k for > 30s then divert to degraded-mode endpoints that limit token length and disable less-critical plugins. That keeps latency SLO for core flows.
[03:35] Luis Chen: We can tolerate degraded-mode for some flows, but not for patient-facing diagnostic text. We need per-route policies.
[03:42] Maya Patel: Absolutely, per-route routing is supported — you can pin routes to the dedicated fleet and set fallback to deny or to a scrubbed hosted variant.
[03:51] Anita Rao: For the dedicated sizing spreadsheet — can you include a column for pre-warmed capacity cost vs cold-provision cost and also hourly burn for a 2-hour burst?
[03:59] Maya Patel: Yes, that's in the action item. We'll also include suggestions from Redwood Optimize on batching thresholds to lower token compute.
[04:08] Tom Becker: Do you have any notes about KV cache eviction tuning? We saw the cache churn when we had many short-lived sessions.
[04:15] Jamal Ortiz: We can tune the TTL and LRU windows; increasing TTL for session prefixes helps, and you can also enable sticky session routing so that the same worker handles a session to get better cache hit. There's a small tradeoff with load distribution.
[04:30] Sofia Marin: On audit logs, we need a redaction policy for PII before logs leave the VPC. Is that supported?
[04:36] Jamal Ortiz: We have server-side redaction hooks and can push sanitized logs to your SIEM; full raw logs can be kept in your VPC if needed.
[04:43] Anita Rao: Great. A couple of quick clarifying items for the runbook: who will own rollback if a burst causes errors?
[04:50] Maya Patel: Redwood will own the serve-side rollback for model variant fallbacks; for infra-level rollbacks your SRE will coordinate with our ops to drain and reprovision. We'll put contact points in the runbook.
[04:59] Tom Becker: Can we also get a short checklist for burst rehearsals — stepwise, e.g., step 1 provision, step 2 smoke test, step 3 ramp to 50% expected, etc.
[05:07] Jamal Ortiz: Yep, that's the burst-runbook-draft.md I linked; I'll tidy it and add exact ramp profiles.
[05:13] Maya Patel: Okay time check, last 5 minutes for recaps and next steps.
[05:18] Anita Rao: Recap from us: we'll send prod traces and confirm the rehearsal attendees. Also need an initial pass at cost numbers.
[05:26] Maya Patel: From Redwood: we'll send updated sizing spreadsheet, cost delta table, and schedule the rehearsal. Jamal will run the KV cache tuning suggestions in staging before the rehearsal.
[05:34] Sofia Marin: We'll review compliance appendix and get back on KMS/keys.
[05:38] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone — I'll follow up with meeting notes and action items.
[05:42] (end)

Notes: Some automated transcription artifacts — product names sometimes spelled 'Redwood Dedicate' or 'Redwood dedicate' in the raw transcript; 'KV' often logged as 'K V'. The team confirmed a Friday rehearsal and delivery dates in the action items above.
